newsitem.title: QATAR: Commercial Bank of Qatar in rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Bank of Qatar in rights issue.

text.p: The Commercial Bank of Qatar (CBQ) said on Sunday it offered 527,342 shares to its shareholders to raise equity capital to participate in the country's gas and industrial development projects.

"To meet the economic growth that we anticipate in the coming years, it is essential that local Qatari banks take measures to strengthen their capital base," said Hussein Alfardan, managing director of the bank.
"To this end we have ammended our constitution to allow an increase in our share capital through a rights issue", he said.
The issue, which opened on Saturday, will close on May 25.
Each shareholder is entitled to subscribe to one new share for every two held at a "preferential" price of 250 riyals ($68.7). CBQ shares, nominally priced at 100 riyals, are currently quoted at 315.
"Any share not taken by existing shareholders will be offered to the public at a price to be determined," Alfardan said.
"On the very first day of the opening of the issue we collected 1.5 million riyals," Mohammad Mandani, deputy general manager said.
Subscriptions from the rights issue will raise the bank's capital to 158.2 million riyals from 105.46 million and the shareholders' equity to 400 million from 130 million.
"This will not only strengthen the bank, it will allow it to participate fully in the ambitious programme of industrial and overall economic development now being undertaken," Alfardan said.
